title: Microsoft Teams: manage Microsoft 365 certified apps through org-wide third-party app settings
summary: The documented controls and their exemptions are supported, and the briefing correctly reports the disagreement between Microsoft's rollout notice and the roadmap. Two small qualifications would improve precision: the Teams licensing exception for anonymous meeting attendance and the scope of Microsoft's promised advance notice.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes administrators enabling Microsoft 365 certified SaaS applications through org-wide third-party app settings.
claims.quote: This feature allows Microsoft 365 administrators to enable Microsoft 365 certified SaaS applications within their tenant through org-wide settings for third-party apps.

claims.claim: The roadmap says administrators can allow a subset of applications verified against industry security and compliance standards.
claims.quote: Admins can choose to allow a subset of applications that have already been verified against industry security and compliance standards.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes maintaining governance and reducing approval overhead.
claims.quote: This ensures organizations can confidently adopt apps while maintaining governance and reducing approval overhead.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope; Open questions; front matter: changes
claims.claim: MC796790 says the certified-app management capability has rolled out completely to all tenants.
claims.quote: This has been rolled out completely for all tenants.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters; rationale: risk and impact
claims.claim: The change is admin-opt-in: Phase 2 does not change org-wide or app-level settings without administrator action.
claims.quote: Note: In this phase, no changes will be applied to org-wide settings or app-level settings without administrator action.

claims.claim: The bulk third-party app control is in Teams admin center at Teams apps > Manage apps > Actions > Org-wide app settings > Third-party apps.
claims.quote: access Teams apps > Manage apps. On Manage apps page, under the Actions menu, select Org-wide app settings. Under Third-party apps, a single control manages the bulk availability of both the new and existing third-party agents and apps.

claims.claim: No PowerShell or Microsoft Graph operation is documented for the org-wide Third-party apps control as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams org-wide Third-party apps control PowerShell Set CsTeamsApp Microsoft Graph teamsAppSettings; "Third-party apps" "PowerShell" "org-wide". Read manage-apps, app-centric-management, teamsAppSettings v1.0/beta; search returned custom-app and permission-policy commands, not this control.

claims.claim: A specific app can be allowed or blocked in Teams admin center at Teams apps > Manage apps > app > Allow or Block.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Teams admin center and access Teams apps > Manage apps. Select the app on the Manage apps page and select Allow or Block option.

claims.claim: MicrosoftTeams PowerShell provides Update-M365TeamsApp -Id <app id> -IsBlocked <Boolean> to change an app's tenant state.
claims.quote: This cmdlet updates app state and app available values for the Microsoft Teams app. -Id: Application ID of Microsoft Teams app. -IsBlocked: The state of the app in the tenant. Type: Boolean

claims.claim: The cmdlet reference's example describes -IsBlocked $true as unblocking an app.
claims.quote:
PS C:\> Update-M365TeamsApp -Id 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b -IsBlocked $true
Unblocks Bookings app (App ID 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b).

claims.where: controls[0].governs and note; What's changing; Governance controls
claims.claim: Learn describes a single tenant-wide control for bulk availability of new and existing third-party apps, subject to app-level exemptions.
claims.quote: these are unified into a single control that governs bulk availability for both new and existing third-party apps. When you toggle ON, all apps are enabled and when you toggle OFF, all apps are disabled. This control doesn't override app-level configurations.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: The Third-party apps control does not override app-level configurations.
claims.quote: This control doesn't override app-level configurations.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: Org-wide defaults apply to new apps and existing apps whose availability administrators have not individually changed.
claims.quote: The Org-wide app settings apply to: All the new apps made available in Teams app store. All the existing apps that you didn't actively manage, that is, you didn't change the availability of.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: Apps individually saved with Specific users and groups assignments are exempt from org-wide defaults.
claims.quote: The Org-wide app settings don’t apply to: All apps that have user assignment set to Specific users and groups and saved by you.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: Apps assigned to Everyone or No one and saved individually are exempt from org-wide defaults.
claims.quote: The Org-wide app settings don’t apply to: All apps that were assigned to Everyone or to No one and saved individually.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: Blocked apps are exempt from org-wide defaults.
claims.quote: The Org-wide app settings don’t apply to: Any blocked apps.

claims.claim: Learn does not document a certified-only option inside the Third-party apps control at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams Microsoft 365 certified apps org-wide settings certified only subset control; "org-wide" "certified" "Third-party apps". Read manage-apps, app-centric-management, overview-of-app-certification and uam-tac-mac; these document filters and bulk defaults, not a certified-only toggle.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The Manage apps page has an Apps to consider allowing tile counting Microsoft 365 certified and publisher-attested apps.
claims.quote: The Teams admin center now includes Apps to consider allowing tile on the Manage apps page. This tile displays counts of Microsoft 365 certified and publisher-attested agents and apps

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Each app's details page has a Security and Compliance tab with certification and security information.
claims.quote: A new Security and Compliance tab on each app’s details page displays its certification status, publisher attestation, and key security attributes etc.

claims.claim: Certification involves developer-provided assessment information and auditing against industry frameworks.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 app compliance program checks and audits an app against controls that are derived from leading industry-standard frameworks. Developers provide answers to a questionnaire ... for Publisher Attestation and for Microsoft 365 certification.

claims.claim: App details pages link to each app's privacy policy.
claims.quote: In Teams admin center, each app page links to the privacy statement and terms of use of the app.

claims.claim: Users can share data with third-party apps made available to them.
claims.quote: A bot can receive messages from users and reply to them. ... This data leaves the corporate network. When a file is sent to a bot, the file leaves the corporate network.

claims.claim: Granting consent to requested app permissions is a separate part of approving an app's use.
claims.quote: Once you decide to approve the use of an app, ensure that the app adoption is smooth for the users. A crucial part of the process is granting consent to the permissions that an app needs to work.

claims.claim: Only a Global admin can consent and apply the final changes in the documented unified-management migration cases.
claims.quote: Only a Global admin can give consent and apply the final changes.

claims.claim: Teams or Global admins can prepare migration updates through the Review summary page.
claims.quote: Any Teams or Global admin can make updates upto the Review summary page.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Saved org-wide app settings take effect after a few hours.
claims.quote: Select Save. The settings take effect after a few hours.

claims.claim: In unified tenants, app status, availability and org-wide settings synchronize between Teams and Microsoft 365 admin centers.
claims.quote: After your tenant is unified, all changes to org-wide settings, agent app, status, or availability in TAC are automatically synchronized in MAC and vice versa.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Each user needs a Teams licence before using Teams.
claims.quote: Except for joining Teams meetings anonymously, each user in your organization must have a Teams license before they can use Teams.
claims.fix: Qualify the licensing sentence and repeated notes as: 'Except for joining Teams meetings anonymously, each user in your organization needs a Teams licence before using Teams.' The exception does not change the licence needed to use the apps discussed here. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/user-access.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Cost and licensing; Scope: Roles
claims.claim: Learn names the Teams Administrator role as the requirement to use Teams admin center.
claims.quote: To use Teams admin center, you must have a Teams Administrator role.

claims.claim: Higher-privilege administrators can perform these governance tasks, but Learn recommends a lower-privilege role.
claims.quote: Some admins with a higher privilege role can accomplish agent and app governance tasks but we recommend using the lower privilege role where possible.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: No separate feature-specific licence is published for the org-wide settings or certified-app management views.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams certified app management org-wide settings licensing price meter additional license. Read manage-apps, user-access, purchase-third-party-apps and overview-of-app-certification; none states a separate licence for these settings or certification views. Roadmap names none.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No feature-specific meter or price is published.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams certified app management org-wide settings licensing price meter additional license. Read manage-apps, user-access, purchase-third-party-apps and overview-of-app-certification; found app subscription costs, not a meter or price for this management feature. Roadmap names none.

claims.claim: The licensing model is included under the general Teams licence requirement, with no published feature-specific entitlement.
claims.quote: Except for joining Teams meetings anonymously, each user in your organization must have a Teams license before they can use Teams.

claims.claim: Some third-party Teams apps require a paid SaaS service subscription.
claims.quote: Some Teams apps require purchasing a service subscription to use app functionality. These service subscriptions are called Software as a Service (SaaS) offers.

claims.claim: Third-party app subscriptions can be bought through AppSource or the Manage apps page.
claims.quote: A license is available for purchase from AppSource and in the Microsoft Teams admin center. You can purchase licenses for services offered by third-party apps from the Manage apps page in the Teams admin center.

claims.claim: Learn says all third-party agents and apps are blocked by default in GCC, GCC High and DoD Teams deployments.
claims.quote: In a Microsoft 365 Government - GCC, GCCH and DoD deployment of Teams, all third-party agents and apps are blocked by default.

claims.claim: Administrators can only view and manage apps deployed in the same release channel as their tenant.
claims.quote: You can only view and manage agents and apps that are deployed in the same release channel as your tenant is.

claims.claim: The single Third-party apps control described here is the post-app-centric-management version.
claims.quote: Before app-centric management migration, org-wide settings had two separate controls for third-party apps ... After migrating to app-centric management, a single control now manages bulk availability for both new and existing third-party apps.

claims.claim: Learn says automatic migration to app-centric management started in April 2025.
claims.quote: Starting from April 2025, your tenant is automatically migrated to app centric management. ... However, until the migration is complete, you can use the wizard and opt to complete the migration manually.

claims.claim: Manage apps says both org-wide and user-level settings must permit an app; app-centric documentation exempts individually managed and blocked apps from org-wide defaults.
claims.quote: To allow an agent or app, you must do all of the following settings. To block an agent or app, use any one of the following settings: Org-wide app settings | Org-level ... App centric managemen | User-level

claims.claim: App permission policies are deprecated for tenants using app-centric management.
claims.quote: Use agent and app assignment through app centric management to define user access for agents and apps. The previous App permission policies is deprecated.

claims.claim: The cited v1.0 teamsAppSettings resource documents two setting properties unrelated to the bulk Third-party apps control.
claims.quote: allowUserRequestsForAppAccess ... Indicates whether users are allowed to request access to the unavailable Teams apps. isUserPersonalScopeResourceSpecificConsentEnabled ... Indicates whether resource-specific consent for personal scope in Teams apps is enabled for the tenant.

claims.claim: The sources document no new autonomous behaviour for this app-availability management feature.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams certified app management 485712 autonomous behaviour availability. Read roadmap, MC796790, manage-apps, app-centric-management, uam-tac-mac and app-permissions. Apps can act autonomously, but no new autonomous execution mechanism is described for this management change.

claims.claim: Microsoft promises at least 60 days' notice for further unified-management changes.
claims.quote: 3. Phase 3 – Automatic Unification (Future) ... We will inform customers of the timeline and additional details at least 60 days in advance before this phase begins.
claims.fix: Replace the last After rollout bullet with: 'Re-read MC796790 and the Learn page for the unified management phases; Microsoft says it will announce the timeline and additional details for Phase 3 automatic availability unification at least 60 days before that phase begins.'

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The Third-party apps default is not limited to certified apps and can make uncertified third-party apps available when enabled.
claims.quote: After migrating to app-centric management, a single control now manages bulk availability for both new and existing third-party apps. Toggle on to enable all new and existing third-party apps across the tenant; toggle off to disable all. App-level settings stay intact.
